sections.title: Part Ⅰ TASK A. Readback and Hearback

body.label: Ground
body.text: HL123, follow the Dash 8 ahead, hold short of Delta.

body.label: Tower
body.text: HL123, cleared for takeoff runway 22, climb to 4,000 feet, report passing 2,000 feet.

body.label: Approach
body.text: HL123, descend to 3,000 feet, cleared for the ILS runway 09 approach, caution birds near the threshold.

body.label: Delivery
body.text: HL123, cleared to Larkin Airport via the DELMA ONE departure, maintain 5,000 feet, squawk 6170.

sections.title: Part Ⅰ TASK B. Checking, Clarifying, Confirming, Informing

body.text: You are at flight level 240 and you have 40 miles left to run to TORIN. To get down from flight level 240 to 11,000 feet you need 43 miles at your present speed. Listen to the controller, respond with a reason, and tell him what you need.

body.label: Center
body.text: HL123, cross TORIN at 11,000 feet.

On final into Carlow you noticed that about four of the approach lights on the left side were out. You were too busy to report it then. You have now landed and the ground controller calls you. Acknowledge the taxi instruction, and report what you saw.

body.label: Ground
body.text: HL123, Carlow Ground, taxi to stand 7 via Golf and Hotel.

Approach instructed you to maintain 2,500 feet until established. You levelled at 2,500 but then got a terrain caution, so you climbed to 3,000 feet and you are there now. Now ATC contacts you. Respond accordingly.

body.label: Approach
body.text: HL123, confirm maintaining 2,500 feet?
3,000 feet / terrain caution

The controller offers you a visual approach to save time. The field is in sight, but it is a dark night with no horizon and you are not familiar with the terrain east of the airport. Listen to the controller, respond with a reason, and tell him what you can accept instead.

body.label: Approach
body.text: HL123, are you able to accept a visual approach?
Delivery gave you squawk 6170 before departure. You set 6107 in the transponder by mistake and it has been running that way since take-off. Now ATC contacts you. Respond accordingly.

body.label: Center
body.text: HL123, verify your squawk.

You have 50 minutes of fuel on board. Your alternate needs 30 minutes from here, and the controller has just given you 20 minutes of holding. That would leave you with no reserve at all. Contact Southgate Control. Point out the problem, and request what you need.
50 on board / alternate 30 / holding 20

sections.title: Part Ⅱ TASK A. Role-play & Follow-up

pre.text: Flight Paths In this scenario, you'll be the pilot flying HL123, which goes through 3 flight stages: Descent, Approach, Taxi.

Initial Situation You are the pilot of HL123, level at flight level 340 and 120 miles from TORIN, en route to Larkin Airport. Your estimate for Larkin is 2252. Larkin has a noise curfew and takes no landings after 2300.

body.text: Contact Southgate Control, report your position and request descent.
Listen to the controller, give a full readback, and inquire what that will do to your arrival time.

body.label: Center
body.text: HL123, Southgate Control, descend to flight level 240, expect 10 minutes of holding at TORIN for the arrival sequence.
Tell the controller what the problem is with the holding, and request what you need, with a reason.

pre.text: Situation Update The controller has given you direct TORIN with no holding, and your estimate is now 2251. You are descending through flight level 180 for 11,000 feet.

body.text: Contact Larkin Approach and report your passing altitude.
Listen to the controller and give a full readback.

body.label: Approach
body.text: HL123, Larkin Approach, good evening, descend to 4,000 feet, reduce speed to 200 knots, expect the TORIN TWO arrival, ILS runway 09, Larkin altimeter 30.04.
Listen to the controller and respond accordingly. Tell him what you need to know before you answer.

body.label: Approach
body.text: HL123, I have a Dash 8 ahead of you doing 160 knots on final, so I may have to slow you down a lot. If that puts you past the curfew, tell me now and I will give you priority.
Listen to the controller and give a full readback.

body.label: Approach
body.text: HL123, cleared for the ILS runway 09 approach, maintain 180 knots to 4 miles, contact Larkin Tower on 119.45.

pre.text: Situation Update You are established on the ILS for runway 09 and passing 1,800 feet. The time is 2248.

body.text: Contact Larkin Tower, report your position and intention.
Listen to the tower and give a full readback. Then inquire how long that taxi will take.

body.label: Tower
body.text: HL123, Larkin Tower, runway 09, cleared to land. After landing, taxiway Golf is closed for works, so expect a long taxi via Kilo.

Follow-up question: You have just finished Task A, as the pilot of Hotel Lima one two three. In this situation, the controller told you to expect 10 minutes of holding when your estimate was already 2252. What was the problem with that, and what did you say to him? In your role as a pilot, how do you handle an airport curfew when you are running late? Give an example of a flight where you would turn back or divert rather than press on.

sections.title: Part Ⅱ TASK B. Extended Role-play : Single Incident/Emergency Related

pre.text: Initial Situation You are the pilot of HL123, descending through flight level 140 for 8,000 feet, inbound to Ashford Airport. You have information Mike.

body.text: Contact Ashford Approach and report your position.
Listen to the controller and give a full readback.

body.label: Approach
body.text: HL123, Ashford Approach, descend and maintain 8,000 feet, reduce speed to 210 knots, expect the VESPA ONE arrival, ILS runway 15, Ashford altimeter 29.76.

pre.text: Situation Update Lowering the gear for the approach you get a red NOSE GEAR UNSAFE indication. You have recycled the gear and used the alternate system, and it still shows unsafe. You have one hour 10 minutes of fuel on board, and there are 186 passengers and 9 crew.

body.text: Inform the controller of your situation, state that you are maintaining 8,000 feet, and request holding while you work the checklist.
Listen to the controller, give a full readback and say your intentions.

body.label: Approach
body.text: HL123, roger, hold at VESPA, left turns, maintain 8,000 feet. Say your intentions when you are ready.
Listen to the controller and provide both pieces of information.

body.label: Approach
body.text: HL123, say your fuel endurance and the number of persons on board.
Listen to the controller. Tell him what you need to know before you decide, then state your intentions with a reason.

body.label: Approach
body.text: HL123, a low pass for a visual check will take about 10 minutes, and the re-approach another 15. Brampton is 35 minutes from here. What would you like to do?

pre.text: Situation Update You have flown the low pass and the tower reports that the nose gear looks down and in place. You now have 55 minutes of fuel on board.

body.text: Contact approach, give them an update, state your decision, and say what you will need on landing.
Listen to the controller and give a full readback.

body.label: Approach
body.text: HL123, roger, turn left heading 180, descend to 2,500 feet until established, cleared for the ILS runway 15 approach, the fire service is in position.
Listen to the controller and provide both pieces of information.

body.label: Approach
body.text: HL123, the tower is asking two things — will you be stopping on the runway, and do you want the fire service alongside or following you?

body.text: What happened to your aircraft (HL123)? Explain the nature of the incident.
How do you think the incident was handled by the air traffic controller? Do you feel the situation could have been handled differently? Make a comment from a pilot's point of view.
